description: Linux's CFS scheduler decomposed. vruntime, red-black tree, nice-weighted timeshare, granularity tuning, group scheduling, wakeup preemption. The mechanism by which Linux gives every task fair CPU time without explicit time slices.

sub_mechanisms.name: vruntime
sub_mechanisms.definition: Per-task counter: time spent on CPU divided by task's weight. Higher-weight tasks accumulate vruntime slower.
sub_mechanisms.why: The core invariant. Scheduler picks lowest-vruntime task. This naturally gives proportional CPU share. Weight comes from nice value: w = 1024 * 1.25^(-nice).

sub_mechanisms.name: red_black_tree_runqueue
sub_mechanisms.definition: Per-CPU red-black tree keyed on vruntime. Leftmost node has the smallest vruntime = next task to run.
sub_mechanisms.why: O(log n) insertion + leftmost lookup. Cache-friendly (small tree of typical workloads). Each CPU has its own runqueue → no global contention.

sub_mechanisms.name: nice_to_weight
sub_mechanisms.definition: Nice value [-20, 19] maps to weight via table. Nice 0 = weight 1024. Each nice step is ~25% weight change. Lower nice = higher priority = higher weight.
sub_mechanisms.why: Nice's geometric weight (~1.25^-n) means consistent proportional effect regardless of starting nice. Going from 0 to 5 is the same ratio as 5 to 10.

sub_mechanisms.name: sched_period
sub_mechanisms.definition: Target time for all runnable tasks to get scheduled once. Default 6 ms scaled by number of tasks. Each task's slice = period × (weight / total_weight).
sub_mechanisms.why: Bounds wait time before next CPU. Too short: thrashing context switches. Too long: poor responsiveness. CFS dynamically scales to keep period reasonable as task count grows.

sub_mechanisms.name: sched_min_granularity
sub_mechanisms.definition: Minimum time a task runs before preemption. Default ~750 µs. Prevents excessive context switching when many tasks present.
sub_mechanisms.why: Without it, sched_period / N tasks would give micro-slices that thrash. min_granularity acts as a floor; many tasks just stretch the period instead.

sub_mechanisms.name: wakeup_preemption
sub_mechanisms.definition: When a sleeping task wakes (e.g., I/O completes), it can preempt the current task if its vruntime is sufficiently lower.
sub_mechanisms.why: Interactive tasks (waiting on input) wake up with low vruntime. Preempting CPU-bound running task gives them fast response. Threshold (wakeup_granularity) prevents thrashing.

sub_mechanisms.name: vruntime_normalisation
sub_mechanisms.definition: When task sleeps, its vruntime is preserved relative to runqueue's min_vruntime. On wakeup, vruntime = max(task's vruntime, min_vruntime - sched_latency/2).
sub_mechanisms.why: Prevents long-sleeping task from monopolising CPU when it wakes (would have very low vruntime). Cap puts it slightly behind currently-running tasks. Maintains fairness across sleep durations.

sub_mechanisms.name: group_scheduling
sub_mechanisms.definition: Tasks grouped (typically per-cgroup or per-user). Schedule between groups proportionally first, then within group.
sub_mechanisms.why: Prevents fork bombs from monopolising CPU. systemd's per-user/per-service cgroups give each user/service equal share. Container CPU quotas implemented via group scheduling.

sub_mechanisms.name: load_tracking
sub_mechanisms.definition: Per-task: tracks running average of CPU + runnable time. Exponential moving average decays load over ~32 ms windows.
sub_mechanisms.why: Per-task 'load' estimate. Used by load balancer to decide migration. Captures recent intensity (vs cumulative which would lag).

sub_mechanisms.name: CPU_load_balancing
sub_mechanisms.definition: Periodic balance: scheduler checks if some CPUs are over/underloaded; migrates tasks to balance. Domain-aware: prefers within socket/core before across.
sub_mechanisms.why: Idle CPU while another's queued tasks waiting = throughput loss. Load balancer respects topology (try to stay in same L3 cache, then same socket). Cost: migration loses cache.

sub_mechanisms.name: isolcpus
sub_mechanisms.definition: Boot parameter excluding specified CPUs from the scheduler's general pool. They run only tasks explicitly affinitized.
sub_mechanisms.why: Reserve cores for latency-critical work (DPDK, real-time audio). Scheduler can't migrate tasks onto isolated CPUs. Effectively partitions the system into general + dedicated cores.

sub_mechanisms.name: schedutil_governor
sub_mechanisms.definition: CPU frequency governor that adjusts based on scheduler load. Replaces ondemand/conservative in modern kernels.
sub_mechanisms.why: Tighter coupling between scheduler + frequency scaling. Lower latency when load increases (no need to wait for separate governor to ramp up). Default on most distros since ~5.x.

derivation_rules.name: CFS_fair_via_vruntime_minimum
if: scheduler always picks the lowest-vruntime task
then: over time, each task accumulates CPU proportional to its weight
derivation_rules.why: Lowest vruntime = least CPU per weight unit. Picking it gives it CPU until another task becomes lowest. Long-run: each task's CPU = weight / sum × total. Mathematical fairness from O(log n) priority queue operations.

derivation_rules.name: sched_period_bounds_max_wait
then: no runnable task waits more than ~T for CPU
derivation_rules.why: All runnable tasks get scheduled within sched_period. Max wait is bounded above by period. Larger period → less context-switch overhead but more wait. CFS's tuning knob for responsiveness vs throughput.

derivation_rules.name: wakeup_preemption_responds_to_interactive_tasks
if: a waking task has substantially lower vruntime than running task
derivation_rules.why: Interactive tasks (sleeping for I/O) wake up rarely → low vruntime accumulation. CPU-bound tasks accumulate vruntime continuously. Preemption favors interactive responsiveness without explicit priority.

derivation_rules.name: group_scheduling_enforces_per_group_quota
if: tasks are organised into scheduling groups
then: each group gets CPU share independent of task count
derivation_rules.why: Without group scheduling, 100 forked tasks would dominate CPU vs 1 task in another group. Group scheduling distributes between groups first. Foundation of container CPU limits.

derivation_rules.name: isolcpus_provides_real_time_guarantees
if: a CPU is isolcpus'd and dedicated tasks run there
then: latency on that CPU is bounded by hardware + driver, not scheduler decisions
derivation_rules.why: Scheduler doesn't migrate other tasks onto isolated CPUs. Dedicated tasks run uninterrupted (except hardware interrupts). Used for HFT, real-time audio, robotics where latency tail matters.
